Journal.Title: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

Article.ArticleTitle: An entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification and molecular characterization in lung adenocarcinoma.

Abstract.AbstractText: Entosis is an actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell process that may culminate in lysosome-mediated entotic cell death and is implicated in tumor evolution. Its clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear.

To construct an Entosis-related Prognostic Prediction Index (EPPI), this study integrated TCGA-LUAD transcriptomic, clinical, and somatic mutation data. Three independent GEO cohorts provided external validation. The initial candidate gene set covered components driving cell-in-cell formation and the intracellular degradation of internalized cells. For subgroup comparison, the analytical approach incorporated survival analysis, functional enrichment, tumor microenvironment profiling, mutation analysis, immunotherapy assessment, and drug-sensitivity prediction. Tissue and cellular distributions of the EPPI genes were mapped using spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing. Molecular docking assessed predicted drug-target interactions. Finally, in vitro RAC1 knockdown experiments evaluated the cellular function of a representative EPPI gene.

Comprising RND3, RAC1, KRAS, CTNNA1, AURKA, and ACTB, the final EPPI consistently stratified overall survival across all cohorts and showed moderate prognostic discrimination. The high-EPPI group had greater tumor purity and mutational burden, with enhanced cell-cycle, DNA-repair, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and NF-κB programs, whereas the low-EPPI group showed greater immune and stromal infiltration. TIDE and immunophenoscores also differed between subgroups. Drug-response models predicted greater sensitivity to cisplatin and paclitaxel in the high-EPPI group and to several targeted agents in the low-EPPI group. Molecular docking predicted RAC1-EHT-1864 and AURKA-alisertib interactions. Spatial and single-cell analyses showed heterogeneous EPPI-gene expression, with ACTB and RAC1 broadly distributed and AURKA restricted to selected populations. RAC1 depletion suppressed LUAD-cell proliferation, DNA synthesis, migration, and invasion.

The EPPI is an entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification in LUAD. Based on this index, patients can be separated into subgroups with distinct proliferative features, genomic alterations, tissue compositions, and predicted drug sensitivities. These findings associate entosis-related molecular features with distinct cellular and clinical characteristics of LUAD.

Article.ArticleTitle: IL18BP links antigen processing and presentation programs to a dendritic cell-enriched immunoregulatory state in colorectal cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: Antigen processing and presentation (APP) is required for tumor immune recognition, but its relationship with the immune landscape in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains incompletely defined. In this study, APP-related transcriptional programs were used as the starting point to identify immune-cell-associated biomarkers with prognostic and immunotherapeutic relevance in CRC.

Six public CRC bulk cohorts were analyzed to define APP-related molecular states. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and four machine-learning frameworks, including Boruta, LassoLR, Pamr, and XGBoost, were applied to prioritize genes linked to APP activity. Single-cell analysis was performed with an atlas of 121 samples and 169,427 cells to identify the cellular origin of the candidate gene. Immune infiltration, cancer-immunity-cycle activity, immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) response, predicted drug response, somatic mutation patterns, and in vitro function were then evaluated.

Two APP-associated patterns were identified and showed different survival outcomes and immune landscapes. Network- and machine-learning-based screening prioritized IL18BP as the main APP-associated candidate. Higher IL18BP expression was associated with longer survival and an immune-active phenotype, including stronger antigen-presentation signals, increased immune infiltration, checkpoint-related signatures, and cancer-immunity-cycle activation. Single-cell profiling showed that IL18BP was preferentially enriched in dendritic cells (DCs), linking the APP-derived bulk signature to a DC-centered immunoregulatory compartment. Across nine external ICB-treated cohorts, IL18BP showed response-classification performance. Drug-response prediction and somatic mutation analyses identified additional features associated with IL18BP-defined groups. In CRC cell lines, IL18BP knockdown increased proliferation, migration, and invasion.

These findings identify IL18BP as a DC-enriched, APP-associated biomarker in CRC. By connecting APP programs in bulk tumors with DC-level expression patterns at single-cell resolution, this study positions IL18BP as an APP-associated marker of a DC-enriched immune state. These findings support further evaluation of IL18BP for prognostic and immunotherapy stratification in colorectal cancer but do not establish a causal APP-DC-IL18BP pathway.

Article.ArticleTitle: AKNA serves as a prognostic biomarker and restrains endometrial cancer progression via STING activation and macrophage reprogramming.

Abstract.AbstractText: AKNA, an AT-hook transcription factor, plays a critical role in cancer development. However, its prognostic value and biological function in endometrial cancer (EC) remain unclear.

To systematically investigate AKNA in EC, we integrated multi-omics data (The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx), and single-cell transcriptomics), dual independent clinical cohorts (TCGA-UCEC dataset and two institutional cohorts), and in vitro/in vivo experimental models. Immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR and Western blotting were used for expression validation. Functional assays, including lentiviral-mediated AKNA knockdown/overexpression, CCK-8, scratch-wound, Transwell, flow cytometry, and colony formation assays were conducted to assess the effects of AKNA modulation on proliferation, migration, invasion, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, chemosensitivity and macrophage polarization. Mechanistically, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) sequencing (ChIP-seq), ChIP-qPCR, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were employed to define the transcriptional regulation of stimulator of interferon genes (STING) by AKNA. A prognostic nomogram integrating AKNA expression with clinicopathological features was developed and externally validated in independent cohorts.

AKNA was significantly downregulated in EC tissues compared with normal endometrium, which was associated with advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, aggressive histological subtypes, and poor prognosis. AKNA knockdown promoted EC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, while enhancing M2 macrophage polarization and reducing sensitivity to paclitaxel and potentially compromising anti-tumor innate immunity. Conversely, AKNA overexpression or STING activation by cyclic GMP-AMP reversed these malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, AKNA directly bound to the STING promoter and transcriptionally activated STING, thereby inducing TANK-binding kinase 1 and interferon regulatory factor 3 phosphorylation. The nomogram combining AKNA with clinicopathological features demonstrated high accuracy in predicting EC recurrence and outperformed single-variable models in both training and validation cohorts.

AKNA deficiency promotes EC progression by transcriptionally suppressing STING and driving M2 macrophage polarization. AKNA serves as a robust prognostic biomarker and predictive indicator for chemotherapy and innate immune modulation, offering a promising therapeutic target for precision treatment of EC.

Article.ArticleTitle: Interpretable machine learning prioritizes transcriptomic features associated with ferroptosis-mitochondrial permeability transition net activity states in cervical cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical carcinogenesis involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and altered non-apoptotic cell-death programs. Ferroptosis and mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT)-driven necrosis may share upstream stress-related transcriptional signals, but their joint pathway-state features in cervical cancer remain incompletely characterized.

We constructed a directionality-aware net pathway activity framework using evidence-audited ferroptosis-promoting, ferroptosis-inhibitory, MPT-promoting, and MPT-inhibitory gene sets in 304 TCGA-CESC primary tumors. The score was benchmarked against ssGSEA, GSVA, and PLAGE and evaluated in controlled simulations. For feature prioritization, score-defining genes were excluded from predictors and Elastic Net feature selection, XGBoost tuning, and model fitting were performed strictly within repeated nested cross-validation. Outer-test SHAP, model-sensitivity analysis, and a 200-permutation complete-pipeline test were used for interpretation and robustness assessment. External validation used GSE138080, GSE63514, GSE223804, and GSE151666.

CombinedNet showed moderate-to-high concordance with ssGSEA, GSVA, and PLAGE (Spearman rho = 0.735, 0.882, and 0.943, respectively), while 1,300 controlled simulations showed strong recovery of the latent promoter-minus-inhibitor balance across scenarios and effect sizes (mean rho = 0.944; mean sign-recovery accuracy = 0.902; mean standardized RMSE = 0.305). The leakage-resistant repeated nested-CV model yielded AUC = 0.780 (95% CI 0.766-0.795); a matched complete-pipeline permutation test gave empirical p = 0.005. Stability-weighted SHAP and perturbation prioritized CKMT1B and KLK13, whereas GNA13, PANX2, and all five sterol genes were not selected in any of 25 outer-fold models. The sterol genes retained modest score correlations but showed no model sensitivity. Across three lesion-progression cohorts, no pathway score remained associated with stage after FDR correction; in the cancer-only GSE151666 RNA-seq cohort, CombinedNet also showed no FIGO-stage trend.

This study supports directionality-aware transcriptomic scoring and a leakage-resistant feature-prioritization framework, but does not support GNA13/PANX2 or cholesterol-biosynthesis signals as stable model drivers or the composite score as a validated lesion-stage biomarker. The findings remain hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Single-cell RNA sequencing combined with artificial intelligence to uncover immunotherapy biomarkers and decipher drug resistance mechanisms in glioblastoma.

Abstract.AbstractText: Glioblastoma represents the most aggressive primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system, characterized by extensive intratumoral heterogeneity, profound immunosuppression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Although immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, its clinical efficacy in GBM remains limited, largely due to the complexity of the tumor ecosystem and the lack of validated predictive biomarkers. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational approaches have provided unprecedented opportunities to decipher tumor heterogeneity and identify clinically actionable biomarkers. This mini-review integrates studies related to scRNA-seq and its combination technology, further elaborating on the tumor plasticity, immune suppression, and metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming mechanisms of GBM. The article systematically summarizes the complete analysis process of integrating single-cell multi-omics data by AI and highlights the application value of AI in validating biomarkers. The above research ideas are expected to overcome clinical resistance problems, optimize patient stratification schemes, and enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy, providing theoretical support for developing highly stable prognostic biomarkers and achieving individualized precise immunotherapy for glioblastoma.

Journal.ISOAbbreviation: Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol

Article.ArticleTitle: Defining GRAMD2 expression in the alveolar epithelium using organoid and single cell approaches.

Abstract.AbstractText: Alveolar epithelial regeneration is critical for normal lung function and disrupted in disease. Precise identification of alveolar epithelial cell populations, particularly type I (AT1) cells, remains a barrier to understanding alveolar homeostasis and repair. We previously identified GRAM domain-containing 2 (GRAMD2) as enriched in distal alveolar epithelium, with predominant expression in type I (AT1) cells. However, recent single-cell datasets reveal low level Gramd2 transcripts in other lung epithelial populations raising questions about specificity. To address this, we performed immunofluorescence of whole lung and cytospins of GFPhigh cells from Gramd2CreERT2;mTmG mice. Cre-induced lineage labeling predominantly marked cells expressing established AT1 markers, with minimal labeling of AT2 or club cells. GFPhigh cells were enriched for AT1 cells and formed organoids in culture that over time showed expression of AT2 and airway markers, suggesting plasticity. Despite apparent purity of the GFPhigh population by immunostaining, single-cell RNAseq identified AT2 cells and a small number of club cells in the labeled population, revealing discordance between GRAMD2 transcript and protein expression. Gramd2CreERT2;mTmG mice enable enrichment of AT1 cells but have limitations for definitive lineage tracing.

Article.ArticleTitle: Limited post-stress recovery and constrained physiological resilience: Multi-biomarker evidence for metabolic trade-offs in a gastropod under ocean acidification.

Abstract.AbstractText: Ocean acidification (OA), driven by increasing atmospheric CO2 absorption, represents a critical environmental stressor that disrupts hepatopancreas function in aquatic organisms, particularly affecting metabolic homeostasis and immune competence. This study employed an integrated multi-biomarker approach combining histopathology, integrated biomarker response (IBR) indices, and transcriptomics to systematically investigate the effects of short-term (14 d), medium-term (28 d) CO2-driven acidification exposure and a subsequent recovery period on the whelk Brunneifusus ternatanus. Hepatopancreatic cells suffered progressive structural and functional damage during 14-28 d of acidification, characterized by reduced hemocyte counts, disruption of rough endoplasmic reticulum membranes, and obscured cell boundaries. During recovery, damage was attenuated yet persistent, manifesting as intracellular matrix edema, hemocyte rebound, and restored membrane integrity-but cell boundaries remained altered relative to controls. The IBR index (integrating oxidative stress markers and hepatopancreas function enzyme indices) increased continuously during early and medium exposure, then decreased significantly during recovery yet remained elevated above control levels, indicating partial but incomplete physiological restoration. Transcriptomic analysis revealed time-specific molecular reprogramming: energy metabolism and mitochondrial function pathways were downregulated during early acidification and recovery stages, whereas medium-term exposure significantly activated immunity- and metabolism-associated pathways. These findings demonstrate that B. ternatanus mounts vigorous physiological regulatory responses to OA stress at a demonstrable energetic cost, characterized by immune-metabolic trade-offs and sustained metabolic reprogramming even after stress removal. This study provides evidence for assessing OA impacts on gastropod mollusks and contributes to predictive frameworks for evaluating marine ecosystem vulnerability under climate change.

Article.ArticleTitle: Longitudinal proteomics integrated with multi‑omics reveal molecular drivers of responses to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in rectal cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is the standard treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), yet its molecular determinants of response remain unclear. We conducted longitudinal 4D-DIA proteomic profiling of pre- and post-treatment specimens from 156 patients, including 31 patients with matched pre- and post-treatment specimens, and integrated with bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation. At baseline, responders were enriched in innate and adaptive immune pathways, whereas non-responders showed proliferative and metabolic programs. Pre-treatment RAC2, elevated in responders, was positively associated with immune activation, oxaliplatin sensitivity, and survival, and was validated in GSE139255 and GSE35640 (all P < 0.05). Moreover, RAC2 demonstrated strong predictive performance (training AUC = 0.867; testing AUC = 0.857). During treatment, NAC induced fibrosis-related remodeling across all groups (all P < 0.05), while responders uniquely preserved CD8⁺ T cell infiltration (P = 0.031). Responders and RAC2-high tumors exhibited concordant pathway dynamics during NAC. Single-cell analysis further revealed that pre-treatment tumor RAC2, higher in responders, transmitted signals to CD8⁺ T cells while receiving inputs from fibroblasts (P < 0.05). In vitro and in vivo, RAC2 knockdown reduced baseline tumor growth but promoted under oxaliplatin (all P < 0.05). Overall, this study offers proteomic insights into NAC in LARC, supports therapeutic decision-making, and identifies potential targets.

Article.ArticleTitle: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus.

Abstract.AbstractText: The thalamus integrates sensory, motor and associative functions through distinct nuclei, yet the developmental principles driving their specification remain unclear. Here we generate a spatiotemporal single-cell multiomic and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the embryonic mouse thalamus, combined with barcoding-based lineage tracing. We identify two major glutamatergic lineages, sensory-related and motor-associative, each governed by different gene regulatory programs and temporal dynamics. These lineages arise from spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor domains, revealing an early segregation of functional identities. Within the sensory lineage, we resolve branching sensory trajectories leading to first-order visual and somatosensory neurons, both emerging from a shared higher-order-like state. Using in silico predictions and in vivo perturbation, we identify Sp9 as a key regulator of visual thalamic fate. Together, our findings define the molecular architecture and developmental trajectories that underpin thalamic modality specification, providing a framework to understand how functional circuits emerge in the mammalian brain.

Article.ArticleTitle: Epigenetic regulation of INPP5D and its downstream molecular network in autoimmune pancreatitis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP) is a representative manifestation of IgG4-related disease characterized by lymphoplasmacytic inflammation and storiform fibrosis. Although epigenetic dysregulation has been implicated in autoimmune diseases, its contribution to the pathogenesis of AIP remains unclear.

Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling was performed using the Infinium MethylationEPIC array in tissues affected by AIP and obstructive pancreatitis (OP). Differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified and subjected to pathway enrichment analysis. Among the significantly enriched gene sets, GNF2_INPP5D showed the strongest enrichment and was selected for further investigation. INPP5D promoter methylation was analyzed, and its protein expression was evaluated by immunohistochemistry. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed to identify the cells expressing INPP5D. Pathway enrichment analysis showed significant enrichment of the INPP5D-associated immune-regulatory network in AIP. Promoter-associated CpG probes within the INPP5D locus showed predominant hypomethylation in AIP compared with the findings in OP (adjusted p < 0.05). In contrast, immunohistochemistry demonstrated reduced INPP5D expression in spindle-shaped stromal macrophage/histiocyte-lineage cells in AIP tissues. scRNA-seq analysis identified INPP5D expression predominantly in C1QC-positive macrophages and lymphocytes.

AIP is characterized by epigenetic remodeling of the INPP5D-associated immune-regulatory network accompanied by reduced INPP5D expression in stromal macrophage-lineage cells. These findings provide evidence for an association between altered INPP5D-related epigenetic regulation and the characteristic fibro-inflammatory microenvironment of AIP. INPP5D may represent a candidate biomarker and a potential therapeutic target in IgG4-related disease.

Article.ArticleTitle: P4HA1⁺ collagen-modifying fibroblasts are associated with pro-tumor niches and therapeutic vulnerabilities in colorectal cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are a major stromal component of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and actively participate in tumor progression. Although CAF heterogeneity in colorectal cancer (CRC) is increasingly recognized, how individual CAF subpopulations simultaneously coordinate extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, angiogenesis, and immune suppression within spatially organized niches remains poorly understood.

CAF heterogeneity was systematically analyzed by integrating single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomic data. By combining cell clustering, pseudotime analysis, transcriptional regulatory network inference, spatial deconvolution, and ligand-receptor interaction analysis, we revealed the spatial distribution and cellular communication characteristics of CAF subpopulations. At the same time, machine learning-based prognostic models and transcriptional perturbation analysis were used to evaluate the clinical significance and potential therapeutic value of CAF-related transcriptional programs.

We identified a prolyl 4-hydroxylase subunit alpha 1 (P4HA1)-positive collagen-modifying CAF subpopulation (P4HA1⁺ CAFs) that was enriched in tumor tissue and exhibited collagen remodeling characteristics. This subpopulation preferentially localized at the tumor-stroma interface, co-localizing with pro-angiogenic endothelial cells, immunosuppressive macrophages, and malignant epithelial cells to form a spatially organized niche with concurrent ECM remodeling, angiogenesis, and immune suppression. P4HA1⁺ CAFs were predicted to engage distinct ligand-receptor axes, including WNT5A-MCAM with endothelial cells, MDK-LRP1 with macrophages, and MDK-NCL with malignant epithelial cells. The MDK-NCL axis was associated with increased RANBP1 expression and enhanced tumor cell proliferation and invasion. Machine learning analysis further identified P4HA1, TIMP1, ARL4C, and SFRP4 as stable core genes associated with poor prognosis. Drug perturbation analysis showed that 2-methoxyestradiol and its combination with the histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor JNJ-26,481,585 may partially reverse the malignant transcriptional program of P4HA1⁺ CAFs.

This study characterizes a P4HA1⁺ collagen-modifying CAF subpopulation that resides within a spatially organized multicellular niche and engages distinct signaling axes to simultaneously promote angiogenesis, immune suppression, and tumor cell proliferation in CRC, highlighting its prognostic and potential therapeutic value.

Article.ArticleTitle: In silico model of axonal pathfinding during spinal cord regeneration in zebrafish larvae.

Abstract.AbstractText: Functional spinal cord repair in zebrafish is governed by regeneration-favorable biochemical and mechanical cues within the lesion microenvironment. Alterations in extracellular matrix composition and stiffness are closely associated with axon regeneration and its failure. However, experimentally dissecting the interplay between mechanical signals and axonal regrowth in vivo remains technically challenging. Here, we present an agent-based modeling framework to simulate stiffness-mediated axonal growth trajectories across the lesion. We use this model to explore potential mechanisms underlying the characteristic growth patterns observed during zebrafish spinal cord regeneration. Experimental growth profiles of regenerated axons were averaged and compared with mean simulation profiles obtained using different mechanosensing parameter sets. Among the tested parameter combinations, a common parameter set yielded the highest profile overlap at 48 hours post lesion. These exploratory comparisons demonstrate that the model can generate selected features of the observed spatial signal distributions of regenerated axons. Hence, our computational framework provides an in silico platform for investigating the role of mechanical cues in axon regeneration in the injured zebrafish spinal cord.

Article.ArticleTitle: From CAF subtypes to clinically relevant states: cancer-associated fibroblasts in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

Abstract.AbstractText: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) develops within a dense, poorly perfused tumor microenvironment (TME) in which cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are prominent cellular and structural components. Once viewed as a uniform population of activated matrix-producing cells, CAFs now include myofibroblastic, inflammatory, antigen-presenting and other populations identified by single-cell and spatial studies. These categories sharpen experimental resolution but do not form a stable hierarchy. CAF phenotypes overlap across spatial niches and disease stages, and they change under metabolic stress or treatment. We frame this heterogeneity as a set of context-dependent functional states. This review synthesizes evidence on fibroblast origins, canonical and recently reported states, and the signals that drive state transitions. It then examines CAF functions in extracellular matrix organization, tumor-cell plasticity and dissemination, metabolic support and immune regulation. Findings on tumor-restraining fibroblasts and protective collagen pools challenge indiscriminate stromal depletion. We also assess CAF states as prognostic and predictive biomarkers, their roles in treatment resistance and therapeutic strategies based on depletion, pathway blockade or stromal normalization. Failures of Hedgehog and hyaluronan-directed therapies show that target abundance alone cannot select patients. Clinical translation will require state definitions that integrate function, spatial context and treatment history, supported by reproducible markers, prospective validation and models that retain human stromal diversity.

Article.ArticleTitle: GeneMamba: Efficient and Effective Foundation Model on Single Cell Data.

Abstract.AbstractText: Transformer-based models have achieved strong performance in single-cell transcriptomics, yet scaling them to genome-wide gene sequences remains challenging due to the quadratic cost of self-attention. Recent state space models (SSMs) offer linear-time sequence modeling, but unidirectional designs may introduce ordering biases and overlook biological structure, potentially limiting robustness across datasets. To address these challenges, we propose GeneMamba, a bidirectional state space model tailored for single-cell RNA sequencing. GeneMamba integrates three key components: (1) Efficiency: BiMamba blocks enable bidirectional processing with O(L) complexity, providing substantial speedup over transformer baselines while maintaining linear scaling; (2) Biological integration: a pathway-aware contrastive objective incorporates curated pathway information to guide representation learning; (3) Scalability: large-scale pretraining on approximately 30 million curated cells (from ~50 million raw CELLXGENE profiles) supports transfer across multiple downstream tasks without task-specific architectures. Across benchmarks including multi-batch integration, cell type annotation, and gene rank reconstruction, GeneMamba demonstrates competitive performance relative to strong baselines such as scGPT and Geneformer, with improvements observed in several settings. Ablation studies further suggest that bidirectional modeling and pathway-aware pretraining contribute to these gains. Overall, GeneMamba provides an efficient and biologically informed framework for foundation modeling in single-cell transcriptomics.

Article.ArticleTitle: Single-cell omics in tracing cellular heterogeneity of drug-induced liver injury: Technological landscape and prospective application.

Abstract.AbstractText: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a serious problem in clinics for both diagnoses and treatment decisions. It is a result of accumulated drugs in human bodies metabolized into toxic constituents generating reactive metabolites, and then arise initial consequences of oxidative stress, organelle stress responses, and lethal consequences (liver necrosis or apoptosis). However, the idiosyncratic nature of DILI complexes its mechanistic studies and still little is known of its potential etiopathogenesis for certain. Single-cell omics technology and approaches serve as powerful tools for investigating cellular heterogeneity and relationships from measurements of up to millions of individual cells at an unprecedented resolution, which are achieved by advances in genome, epigenome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolism technologies. As liver contains heterogeneous cell types of distinct spatial, molecular, and functional properties, they interact with each other to precede cell type-specific omics reprogramming and play an irreplaceable role in liver cells with heterogeneous properties upon encountering toxic insults. Single-cell omics, especially single-cell transcriptomics and single-cell proteomics, have been utilized for exploring the mechanisms of DILI and prediction for risk factors. In this review, we discuss the recent development and future perspectives of single-cell omics-based technologies for DILI-related research.

Article.ArticleTitle: Thyroid Differentiation Score as a Molecular Bridge Between Genotype, Tumor Biology, and Radioiodine Theranostics in Thyroid Cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: Differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) is characterized by retention of thyroid-specific functions, particularly iodide uptake mediated by the sodium-iodide symporter (NIS), which underlies the effectiveness of radioiodine (RAI) imaging and therapy. Loss of iodine avidity reflects tumor dedifferentiation and is a defining feature of aggressive, RAI-refractory disease. The Thyroid Differentiation Score (TDS), introduced by The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) program, provides a quantitative transcriptomic measure of thyroid lineage identity based on coordinated expression of genes involved in thyroid hormone biosynthesis and transport. This comprehensive narrative review synthesizes current evidence supporting TDS as a unifying framework linking oncogenic drivers, signaling pathways, tumor microenvironment, metabolic reprogramming, and clinical behavior across thyroid cancer subtypes, including papillary, follicular, poorly differentiated, anaplastic, and pediatric tumors. MAPK pathway activation, particularly via BRAFV600E, is associated with suppression of thyroid differentiation programs, whereas RAS-like and fusion-driven tumors tend to retain higher differentiation states. Emerging data connect TDS with tumor aggressiveness, recurrence risk, immune and inflammatory signaling, and resistance to RAI therapy. The role of TDS in guiding redifferentiation strategies using targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors is also discussed, highlighting its potential as a biomarker for patient selection in RAI re-sensitization approaches. TDS is a well-established biological measure of thyroid-lineage differentiation and has shown prognostic associations in retrospective studies. However, its value as an individual predictive or theranostic biomarker remains investigational. Future work should focus on developing a personalized theranostic TDS that integrates matched normal tissue, molecular profiling, functional imaging, and machine learning to potentially better predict iodine-handling capacity and optimize precision management in thyroid cancer.

Article.ArticleTitle: Single-Cell Dissection of Inflammatory Suppression and Stemness Plasticity Reveals STMN1-Associated Malignant Epithelial Cells in Severe Lung Cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: The disease course in patients with advanced lung cancer with malignant serous effusions (ALC-MSE) is complex, and treatment outcomes are difficult to predict; systematic studies on the tumor stem cell-like characteristics and regulatory mechanisms of this condition are still lacking. Based on single-cell transcriptomic data and the TCGA-LUAD cohort, this study systematically analyzed the functional characteristics and key regulatory networks of malignant epithelial cells in severe lung cancer. Key findings include: epithelial cells in severe lung cancer exhibit significantly attenuated inflammation- and immunity-related signaling pathways (including NF-κB, TNF, and JAK-STAT signaling pathways), enhanced stem cell-like properties, and metabolic reprogramming; we identified a highly stem-like malignant epithelial cell subpopulation, represented by Cluster 3, which is enriched in stem-like pathways such as Notch, Hippo, TGF-β, and FoxO, and is accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial metabolism and stress adaptability; STMN1 is a key molecule regulating this stem-like state, showing a significant positive correlation with stemness scores and mRNAi; cells with high STMN1 expression gain a survival advantage and may maintain their stemness by attenuating CAF/ECM signaling with other cells (COL1A1-CD44), inhibiting complement activation and antigen presentation signaling (such as C3, ANXA1, and MHC-II-related molecules), and enhancing stemness niche signaling (MIF-CD74/CD44). Furthermore, NELFE, MYBL2, FOXN3, POLR2A, and RAD21 were identified as potential upstream regulators of STMN1. In vitro experiments confirmed that, following induction of stem cell-like properties, STMN1 was significantly overexpressed in lung adenocarcinoma cells, accompanied by upregulation of related stem cell markers (SOX2, NANOG, OCT4, and CD44). In summary, this study reveals a significantly enhanced stemness state in malignant epithelial cells in advanced lung cancer, accompanied by suppressed inflammatory signaling and enhanced metabolic adaptation, and identifies STMN1 as a key molecule driving stemness maintenance and disease progression.

Article.ArticleTitle: Stem Cell and EV/sEV Strategies for Neuroimmune Niche Reprogramming in Selected CNS Disorders: Mechanisms, Engineered Delivery, and Translational Readiness.

Abstract.AbstractText: Aging has traditionally been interpreted through the accumulation of oxidative damage. However, reactive oxygen species (ROS) also act as regulated signals that support immune activation, metabolic adaptation, stress resistance, inflammatory resolution, and cell-fate decisions. We define redox signaling fidelity as the accuracy with which a specified physiological input is converted into a source-specific, spatially confined, temporally patterned, chemically reversible, proportionately decoded, and appropriately resolved redox response.

This critical narrative review develops redox signaling fidelity as a testable systems framework rather than as a synonym for oxidative stress, redox homeostasis, oxidative eustress, hormesis, the redox code, or Redox-stress Response Capacity. The framework organizes redox information flow into five linked layers: generation, encoding, transmission, decoding, and resolution/reset. Aging may lower fidelity through source uncoupling, persistent cysteine oxidation, microdomain leakage, decoder bias, and defective autophagic, mitophagic, lysosomal, or proteostatic reset. Immune aging and the aging brain are used as cross-scale test cases in which physiological ROS pulses must be distinguished from chronic redox noise. We propose operational readouts, including source coupling, redox signal-to-noise ratio, reversibility, spatial leakage, decoder proportionality, mutual information, and resolution kinetics, and map these readouts to single-cell imaging, redox proteomics, spatial and single-cell omics, and dynamic modeling.

The fidelity framework predicts that lowering bulk ROS is not sufficient to restore redox function. More decisive studies should pair controlled inputs with compartment-resolved redox dynamics, reversible molecular encoding, pathway output, and functional recovery in the same young-versus-aged system. Interventions should be evaluated by whether they reduce pathological redox noise while preserving physiological pulses, spatial routing, adaptive decoding, and timely resolution.

Article.ArticleTitle: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance.

We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 92,218 cells across 13 treatment-naïve BLCA samples to characterize epithelial stemness and tumor-microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics and independent bulk cohorts were used for orthogonal and clinical validation. An HStem-associated histopathology-based prognostic model was developed by integrating quantitative image features with deep-learning representations, followed by functional validation of the candidate gene C11orf24.

We identified a highly stem-like epithelial population (HStem) at the apex of the differentiation hierarchy, exhibiting MYC activation, oxidative phosphorylation, and DNA repair enrichment, with preferential presence in advanced-stage tumors. HStem cells were inferred to serve as major communication hubs within the TME, interacting extensively with fibroblasts and endothelial cells via MIF-CD74/CXCR4 and MIF-CD74/CD44 axes. An 86-gene HStem signature enabled development of a robust image-based prognostic model. High-risk tumors showed immune exclusion, immunosuppressive enrichment, T-cell dysfunction, and predicted checkpoint blockade resistance. C11orf24 emerged as a candidate stemness-associated regulator; C11orf24-positive cells displayed enhanced stemness and stromal interactions. Functional experiments demonstrated that C11orf24 perturbation altered clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in BLCA cells. Pharmacogenomic analyses identified predicted therapeutic vulnerabilities that warrant experimental validation.

We identify an HStem population associated with BLCA progression, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evasion. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with computational pathology, we establish a clinically relevant stemness framework and identify C11orf24 as a potential therapeutic target, offering opportunities for stemness-directed precision oncology.

Journal.Title: Expert opinion on drug metabolism & toxicology

Article.ArticleTitle: Obstetric pharmacotranscriptomics.

Abstract.AbstractText: Pregnancy produces gestational-age and tissue-specific transcriptional remodeling in maternal blood, placenta, decidua, fetal membranes, and fetal compartments that can modify pathways governing drug disposition and response. Obstetric pharmacotranscriptomics seeks to relate these dynamic expression states to medication exposure, target engagement, efficacy, and toxicity.

This narrative review defines obstetric pharmacotranscriptomics, distinguishes pregnancy- and disease-associated expression from medication-induced transcriptional effects, and evaluates current evidence from maternal blood, cell-free RNA, placenta, and pregnancy-relevant experimental models. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from database inception through 15 September 2026, using combinations of pregnancy, placenta, transcriptomics, RNA sequencing, pharmacotranscriptomics, drug response, medication exposure, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, cytochrome P450, UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (uridine 5'-diphospho-glucuronosyltransferase), ATP-binding cassettes, solute carrier transporters, and specific obstetric medications. Priority was given to human pregnancy studies, longitudinal designs, direct drug-perturbation experiments, and mechanistically informative preclinical studies.

Pregnancy transcriptomics is substantially more mature than pregnancy pharmacotranscriptomics. The strongest path forward is to embed longitudinal transcriptomic sampling within pharmacokinetic and therapeutic studies so that gestational biology, drug exposure, target engagement, efficacy, and toxicity can be distinguished. Clinically useful signatures will require independent validation, tissue and cell-type specificity, demonstrated incremental value over standard clinical predictors, and conversion to reproducible targeted assays.

Article.ArticleTitle: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells.

Abstract.AbstractText: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

Article.ArticleTitle: BCL2A1 marks an early, less-exhausted CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte state associated with PD-1 blockade response in NSCLC.

Abstract.AbstractText: The tumor microenvironment exerts intense survival pressure on CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), yet the cellular basis for an earlier, less-exhausted state associated with response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. We previously identified BCL2A1 as a CD8+ TIL-derived marker predictive of a response to PD-1 blockade. Here we combine deep single-cell discovery with experimental validation in primary human T cells to characterise the BCL2A1-associated CD8+ TIL state and its candidate upstream signal.

We integrated four transcriptomic cohorts-pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq with CD8+ TIL deconvolution (n=60), on-treatment scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=11), longitudinal scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=18), and an independent post-treatment cohort (n=59)-with in silico perturbation, pathway, and metabolic-flux analyses, and experimentally tested a key prediction of this state by flow cytometry in primary human CD8+ T cells.

BCL2A1 high CD8+ TILs showed elevated BCL2A1 expression without coordinated upregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2-family genes, maintained minimal exhaustion, and occupied an early, BCL6-, TCF7-, and NFKB1-regulated pseudotime state. Across longitudinal and post-treatment cohorts, they formed diverse, low-expansion repertoires rather than dominant expanded clones, with reduced biosynthetic flux (branched-chain amino acid and purine metabolism) consistent with a non-proliferative state. NF-κB signaling was elevated, and TNF-α was nominated as the leading candidate upstream ligand of BCL2A1. We then experimentally tested this prediction: in primary human CD8+ T cells, TNF-α induced BCL2A1 protein ≈13-fold (44.5% vs. 3.4% BCL2A1+; MFI 2.93-fold; P < 0.0001), whereas CD3/CD28 activation alone did not, establishing a TNF-α-specific, protein-level response.

Combining integrative single-cell analysis with experimental validation in primary human T cells, we define BCL2A1 as a marker of an early, less-exhausted CD8+ TIL state associated with improved ICB outcomes in NSCLC; a survival-related role is supported by these associations but was not functionally tested.

Article.ArticleTitle: Integrating transcriptomic analysis and experimental validation unravels autophagy- and lactylation-related gene signatures in acute myocardial infarction.

Abstract.AbstractText: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is a leading global health burden. While autophagy and lactylation are crucial in cardiovascular pathophysiology, their coordinated roles in AMI remain unclear. This study investigates the transcriptional signatures associated with both processes to identify diagnostic biomarkers.

Transcriptomic datasets (GSE66360, GSE48060), autophagy-related genes (ARGs), and lactylation-related genes (LRGs) were analyzed. Differentially expressed ARGs and LRGs (DE-ARGs, DE-LRGs). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) pinpointed key module genes correlated with their activity scores. Biomarker selection employed protein-protein interaction networks, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, artificial neural network (ANN) model, and validation in clinical samples.

WGCNA identified 1,442 key module genes. ATM and STAT1 were validated as robust diagnostic biomarkers. Models built with these genes showed high diagnostic accuracy in independent cohorts. Functional enrichment implicated the neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction pathway. Immune infiltration analysis revealed a statistically significant negative correlation between ATM/STAT1 expression and eosinophil infiltration levels (cor=-0.42, p < 0.05), suggesting a potential association. Rat models showed a trend toward downregulation of both biomarkers in AMI, although these findings require validation in larger cohorts due to the limited sample size (n = 4 per group).

This integrative study identifies ATM and STAT1 as promising diagnostic biomarkers for AMI, with their expression signatures robustly correlated with both autophagy- and lactylation-associated gene activity scores. These findings provide a foundation for further investigation into the potential roles of these genes in linking metabolic reprogramming and inflammatory responses in AMI.

Article.ArticleTitle: Integrated analyses identify MAN1B1 as a candidate regulator of chemotherapeutic tolerance and immunosuppression in bladder cancer.

Abstract.AbstractText: Gemcitabine (GEM) resistance limits treatment efficacy in bladder cancer (BC). This study identified MAN1B1 as a key driving factor for chemotherapy resistance and malignant progression in BC.

Bulk-RNA datasets GSE190636 and single-cell RNA-seq dataset GSE250523 from GEO. Use limma package to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the process of GEM resistance, and then perform GO and KEGG enrichment analysis. Screening candidate targets through molecular docking with GEM, and further evaluation through molecular dynamics simulation and GEPIA survival analysis. GSEA analysis is used to explore pathways associated with key genes. Perform single-cell analysis using Seurat, SingleR, Monocle 2, CellChat, and scTenifoldKnk, including cell annotation, pseudo time trajectory, intercellular communication, and virtual knockout. Carry out functional experiments in bladder cancer cell lines, including cell viability, wound healing Transwell, Colony formation and Western blot analysis.

Through comprehensive transcriptome analysis and single-cell sequencing, we found that elevated levels of MAN1B1 are associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Computational molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations indicate the potential binding interaction between MAN1B1 and GEM.This enzyme orchestrates a dual microenvironmental reprogramming by hyperactivating metabolic cascades while simultaneously dampening anti-tumor immune surveillance, predominantly originating from the epithelial compartment to modulate intercellular crosstalk. Functional disturbance experiments showed that knockout of MAN1B1 was associated with decreased cell survival, migration, and invasion, as well as increased sensitivity to GEM, while ectopic expression of MAN1B1 increased cell survival and was associated with enhanced PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activity.

Our findings uncover the multifaceted regulatory network governing MAN1B1, establishing its utility as an innovative prognostic indicator and an actionable therapeutic vulnerability for overcoming GEM insensitivity in urological oncology.

Article.ArticleTitle: Spatiotemporal Immune-Fibroblast Crosstalk in Pulmonary Fibrosis: From Failed Repair to Fibrotic Niche Formation.

Abstract.AbstractText: Pulmonary fibrosis is a common and often fatal outcome of fibrosing interstitial lung diseases, characterized by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, destruction of alveolar architecture and irreversible loss of respiratory function. Although fibroblast activation and epithelial dysfunction are central to disease pathogenesis, fibrosis cannot be adequately explained by mesenchymal dysregulation alone. Rather, it represents a failure of multicellular repair regulation, in which immune cells, fibroblasts and epithelial populations reciprocally reshape cellular states, tissue niches and disease trajectories. Early innate immune responses amplify epithelial injury while simultaneously initiating provisional repair; however, when injury persists, these transient programmes fail to resolve and become stabilized into chronic profibrotic circuits involving monocyte-derived macrophages, dysfunctional T cells, inflammatory fibroblasts and matrix-producing myofibroblasts. Recent single-cell, spatial transcriptomic and lineage-tracing studies have revealed discrete cellular states, including SPP1⁺ scar-associated macrophages, inflammatory fibroblasts, CTHRC1⁺ myofibroblasts and tertiary-lymphoid-structure-associated stromal cells, that assemble multicellular, stage-specific and microanatomically restricted fibrotic niches. Collectively, these findings support a model in which soluble mediators, extracellular matrix mechanics, metabolic rewiring and immune-regulatory signalling cooperate to establish self-reinforcing stromal-immune circuits. In this Review, we synthesize current evidence for bidirectional immune-fibroblast crosstalk in pulmonary fibrosis, focusing on macrophage and T cell programmes, fibroblast-mediated immune regulation, spatiotemporal niche remodelling, mechanistic signalling networks, experimental models and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that progressive fibrosis reflects the spatiotemporal locking of pathological epithelial-immune-stromal circuits, a framework that may explain the limited efficacy of broad anti-inflammatory therapies in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and guide the development of more precise, stage-specific and combinatorial antifibrotic strategies.

Article.ArticleTitle: Computational Prediction of the Therapeutic Mechanisms From the Turmeric-Pueraria-Coix Seed Botanical Formula in Rheumatoid Arthritis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by progressive synovial inflammation and immune-metabolic reprogramming. The polyphenol-rich Turmeric-Pueraria-Coix seed (TPC) formula shows therapeutic potential against RA, though its multi-target mechanisms remain uncharacterized. To explore how TPC modulates ferroptosis and oxidative stress in RA, we integrated systems nutrition network analysis with multicohort transcriptomic datasets to identify candidate targets. Ensemble machine learning algorithms and independent cohort validation prioritized key biomarkers. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations evaluated the dynamic behavior and interaction persistence of polyphenol-target complexes, and single-cell in silico overexpression and knockout analyses characterized the regulatory consequences of perturbing these targets within RA synovial networks. Analysis identified 85 bioactive phytochemicals in the TPC formula, forming a polyphenol-dominant matrix mapping to 40 RA targets. Algorithmic and cross-cohort prioritization isolated six core genes (ALOX5, CD38, CDK1, EZH2, MAPK8, and PTGS2) linked to RA synovial transcriptomic patterns, with varying predictive performance across external cohorts. SHAP analysis highlighted PTGS2, CD38, and MAPK8; however, MD simulations prioritized CD38 and MAPK8 as stable targets of coumestrol, whereas PTGS2 exhibited less dynamic stability. Single-cell perturbation analysis revealed similar regulatory responses following MAPK8 and PTGS2 modulation, whereas CD38 knockout produced a distinct network response. These findings link TPC-derived polyphenols to CD38/MAPK8 signaling and ferroptosis in RA, providing testable molecular hypotheses for experimental validation.

Article.ArticleTitle: Identification of Immuno-Diagnostic and Therapeutic Markers in Tumors and Inflammatory Diseases Based on Single-Cell and Machine Learning Methods.

Abstract.AbstractText: Chemotherapy is the mainstay of systemic treatment for colorectal cancer (CRC), but drug resistance and tumor heterogeneity markedly limit survival. Mitochondrial metabolism is increasingly recognized as a regulator of tumor progression, immune contexture, and therapeutic response. However, the prognostic relevance of mitochondrial metabolism-related transcriptional patterns and their relationships with chemotherapy-response signatures and immune features in CRC remain incompletely understood.

Clinical and transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas colorectal cancer cohort (TCGA-CRC) and Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts GSE17537 and GSE104645 were analyzed. A curated set of mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MMRGs) were used to calculate an MMRG score, whereas genes upregulated in chemotherapy-sensitive cases in GSE104645 were used to derive a drug-sensitivity gene-set score by single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA). Weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA), differential expression analysis, univariate Cox regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and multivariate Cox regression were used to construct a five-gene RiskScore. Prognostic associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, external validation, and subgroup analyses. Immune-cell enrichment and pRRophetic-predicted half-maximal inhibitory concentration values were evaluated, and CD36 was examined using in vitro phenotypic assays.

Tumors showed lower MMRG scores than normal tissues, and higher MMRG scores were associated with better overall survival (OS). The drug-sensitivity gene-set score was higher in tumors but was not significantly associated with OS. A five-gene signature (CD36, CPA3, FCRL2, POU2F2, and S100B) generated a RiskScore that separated OS outcomes in the TCGA training, testing, and overall cohorts, as well as GSE17537, although its time-dependent discrimination varied across cohorts and follow-up periods. Similar survival associations were observed within subgroups defined by stage, age, and sex; however, independent or incremental prognostic value was not evaluated. High-risk tumors exhibited altered immune-cell enrichment, and the RiskScore was correlated with pRRophetic-predicted drug IC50 values after Benjamini-Hochberg correction. CD36 expression was higher in SW1116 than in NCM460 cells, and its knockdown inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion. Mitochondrial function was not directly measured in these experiments.

The five-gene RiskScore was associated with OS, immune-cell enrichment, and in silico drug-sensitivity estimates in CRC. It may serve as a candidate tool for prognostic stratification, but its incremental clinical value and treatment-predictive utility require prospective validation. The CD36 knockdown experiments support a tumor-promoting phenotype in SW1116 cells but do not establish dependence on mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming.

Article.ArticleTitle: An Eight-Gene Metabolic Prognostic Signature in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Cross-Cohort Evaluation, Single-Cell Analysis, and Preliminary Functional Evaluation of PYGL and G6PD.

Abstract.AbstractText: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the most prevalent pathological subtype of head and neck malignancies. Although metabolic reprogramming contributes to malignant progression and adaptation within the tumor microenvironment in HNSCC, its biological and prognostic implications remain incompletely understood.

To develop and evaluate a metabolism-related prognostic score for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) across multiple cohorts, identify its cellular sources at single-cell resolution, and perform preliminary in vitro functional evaluation of PYGL and G6PD.

Metabolism-related differentially expressed genes were screened in The Cancer Genome Atlas Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma cohort (TCGA-HNSC). A total of 506 patients with survival data were divided into a training set (n = 355) and an internal test set (n = 151) at a 7:3 ratio. Training-only repeated nested cross-validation benchmarked 126 algorithmic configurations. Survival-SVM had the highest mean out-of-fold C-index, whereas an eight-gene LASSO + StepCox model was retained for interpretability and cross-cohort transportability. External cohort evaluation of overall survival (OS) was performed in GSE65858 (n = 270), while GSE117973 (n = 77), which used disease-specific survival (DSS), was treated as an exploratory cohort. By integrating 54,163 single cells from the GSE150321 and GSE172577 datasets, analyses, including inferCNV, 12 predefined metabolic modules, CellChat, and scTenifoldKnk, were conducted to investigate the cellular origins of the risk score and candidate regulatory networks; additionally, PYGL- and G6PD-targeting siRNAs were evaluated for their effects on target protein expression and wound closure in vitro.

We developed a metabolic prognostic model that included HPRT1, ADA, PYGL, P4HA1, LDHA, G6PD, NT5E, and FTH1. The concordance indices (C-indices) were 0.638 in the TCGA training set, 0.651 in the internal test set, and 0.604 in GSE65858. In a complete-case clinical cohort of 473 TCGA patients, a model combining the risk score with age, sex, and T, N, and M categories achieved C-indices of 0.693 in TCGA and 0.677 in GSE65858. The corresponding 3-year areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.735 and 0.700. Single-cell analysis showed that the eight genes were distributed across malignant epithelial, proliferating, immune, endothelial, and stromal populations. The 16,240 copy number variation-high (CNV-high) epithelial cells had higher eight-gene scores and higher transcriptional scores for glycogen metabolism, the pentose phosphate pathway, glycolysis, and redox-related programs. Small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated silencing of G6PD or PYGL reduced relative wound closure at 12 h in TU686 and SCC25 cells.

The eight-gene metabolic score provided moderate and cohort-dependent prognostic discrimination in the TCGA internal test set and GSE65858. Its bulk transcriptomic signal arose from several cell populations. Silencing PYGL or G6PD reduced target protein expression and wound closure. These findings provide preliminary in vitro evidence linking both genes to a migratory phenotype in HNSCC.

Article.ArticleTitle: Integrative topological and longitudinal transcriptomic analyses identify a 14-gene interferon-stimulated module associated with acquired sunitinib resistance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

Abstract.AbstractText: Acquired sunitinib resistance poses a major clinical challenge in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). We integrated cross-model transcriptomic analysis of resistant cell lines, multi-algorithm protein-protein interaction screening, longitudinal patient-derived xenograft (PDX) profiling, and clinical ccRCC tissue analysis. This framework prioritized a 14-gene interferon-stimulated module that was concordantly upregulated in A498 and 786-O resistant sublines and showed coordinated activation during the therapeutic escape phase in a PDX model. Pathway enrichment linked the module to type I/II interferon signaling and antiviral defense. In cross-sectional clinical ccRCC tissues without annotated sunitinib treatment histories, the module was also more highly expressed than in normal kidney and displayed altered co-expression patterns. This finding supports disease-associated activation but does not establish resistance specificity. Collectively, the data identify a tumor-cell-intrinsic component associated with acquired sunitinib resistance and temporally aligned with therapeutic escape. Functional perturbation and longitudinal patient studies are required to determine causality and predictive value.

Article.ArticleTitle: GM2A links keratinocyte metabolism to inflammation in psoriasis: Integrated transcriptomic and functional analyses.

Abstract.AbstractText: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis driven by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation and extensive immune cell infiltration. Emerging evidence links its pathogenesis to lipid metabolic dysregulation, yet the specific molecules bridging lipid remodeling to immune activation remain largely unknown. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic datasets through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential expression analysis, and ensemble machine learning (random forest [RF] and support vector machine recursive feature elimination [SVM-RFE]), identifying ganglioside GM2 activator (GM2A) as a top lipid metabolism-related hub gene. Multi-cohort validation confirmed its robust upregulation in psoriatic lesions and its responsiveness to anti-psoriatic therapies. Furthermore, GM2A expression positively correlated with PASI scores and demonstrated strong diagnostic power in a nomogram-based model, reinforcing its candidacy as a diagnostic biomarker. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that GM2A is specifically elevated in spinous keratinocytes, where it drives ganglio-series glycosphingolipid reprogramming. Intercellular communication analysis demonstrated that spinous keratinocytes promote inflammatory infiltration primarily through the macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-CD74 signaling axis, targeting T cells and myeloid cells. In an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, GM2A was significantly upregulated and predominantly localized to the thickened spinous layer, accompanied by elevated levels of inflammatory cytokines. In M5-induced HaCaT cells, GM2A knockdown reduced the mRNA levels of IL-17 A, TNF, IL-6, and IL-1β, attenuated p65 phosphorylation, and decreased MIF release into the supernatant. Additionally, molecular docking identified cyclosporine A as a potential direct binder of GM2A with high affinity. Collectively, our study delineates a novel GM2A-driven metabolic-immune axis in psoriasis, positioning GM2A as a potential diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

Article.ArticleTitle: Polystyrene Microplastics Exacerbate Arsenic-Induced Ferroptosis and Lipid Metabolism Dysregulation in Chicken Hepatocytes through SIRT7-SIRT1 Axis-Associated Transcriptomic Alterations.

Abstract.AbstractText: Co-contamination with arsenic (As) and polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) poses a significant risk to environmental health. This study elucidated the synergistic toxicity mechanism of PS-MPs and As using a chicken hepatocyte model, integrating electron microscopy, migration assays, and comprehensive biomarker assessment. Toxicity prediction, molecular docking, transcriptomics, protein-protein interaction networks, and Pearson correlation analysis were further employed to clarify the underlying mechanism of their combined toxic effects. Molecular docking analysis provided supporting computational evidence that the styrene monomer derived from PS-MPs interferes with antioxidant proteins (e.g., SIRT1), suggesting a possible mechanism by which PS-MPs could exacerbate intracellular As accumulation. This interaction precipitates a vicious cycle of oxidative stress and lipid metabolism disorders. Further research has found that synergistic toxicity was significantly associated with a coordinated dysregulation of SIRT7 and SIRT1, suggesting a perturbation of the dynamic balance between these two regulators. This imbalance subsequently suppresses PPAR-α signaling and GPX4, while upregulating lipid accumulation markers and ferroptosis drivers such as ACSL4. These findings, together with functional validation via SIRT1 overexpression and SIRT7 knockdown, identify a potential core regulatory axis of the SIRT7-SIRT1 protein network in the synergistic toxicity of As-PS-MPs. Our research provides a new framework for the toxicological analysis of PS-MPs and As through transcriptomics and bioinformatics analysis and offers new ideas for further studies on combined pollutant exposure.

Article.ArticleTitle: Nonhistone Protein Acetylation Reprograms the ECM-Receptor Interaction Pathway: Multiomics Profiling of Cartilage Degeneration in Rat Models of Osteoarthritis.

Abstract.AbstractText: Nonhistone acetylation is a key epigenetic mechanism in osteoarthritis (OA), but its specific role in cartilage degeneration remains unclear. Here, we integrated transcriptomics, proteomics, and acetyl-proteomics to systematically analyze molecular changes in rat OA cartilage. Multiomics coenrichment identified the ECM-receptor interaction pathway as the core target, reprogrammed by increased acetylation of Fn1, Tnc, and Itgb1. Using 113 machine-learning strategies, we identified 11 core diagnostic genes, with Wisp3 showing the highest efficacy validated in independent data sets. In vitro experiments and single-cell RNA-seq confirmed that Wisp3 downregulation disrupts ECM homeostasis. This study reveals that nonhistone acetylation drives OA by reprogramming the ECM-receptor interaction pathway and provides novel early diagnostic biomarkers.

Article.ArticleTitle: Dose-specific reprogramming of the mucociliary-humoral immune interface in oysters upon biodegradable microplastics exposure.

Abstract.AbstractText: Poly(lactic acid) microplastics (PLA-MPs) have been widely regarded as alternatives to conventional plastics, but their cellular effects on marine filter-feeders remain poorly understood. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to resolve the early gill responses of Hong Kong oyster (Crassostrea hongkongensis) after 7 days of UV-aged PLA-MPs exposure at two different concentrations. PLA exposure triggered significant dose remodeling along the mucus-cilia-humoral immune particle processing pathway, among which the humoral immune characterized by mature soluble recognition functions displayed the highest sensitivity, acting as the potential early response indicators for the PLA-MPs. At the low dose, mucous cells first initiated transcriptional reprogramming related to physicochemical regulation, whereas ciliated cells showed a decoupled motility-directionality. Meanwhile, the mature humoral recognition gate weakened, and the residual immunes state shifted to local coating and containment. At the high dose, mucous cells exhibited higher oxidative metabolism and glycoprotein processing demands. Motile and polar-related ciliary states decreased, while junction remodeling states accumulated and formed a maturation bottleneck in ciliated cells. Humoral immunity further shifted from mature recognition to proteolytic regulation. Cell-cell communication suggested dose specific reorganization of homology supported signaling networks, with ionocyte-associated interactions more prominent at the low dose and sensory epithelium and junctional barrier interactions more prominent at the high dose; these predicted interactions require further functional validation. Taken together, these findings defined a nonlinear transition from low-dose physicochemical interface adaptation to high-dose particle burden associated mucociliary-immune remodeling, providing a cellular and mechanistic basis for identifying early biological effects and assessing the ecological risks of biodegradable microplastics in estuarine bivalves.

Article.ArticleTitle: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition.

Abstract.AbstractText: Biological systems exhibit complex hierarchical regulation, with interactions across multiple layers governing transitions between states. Identifying the causal architecture underlying these state transitions remains challenging because confounding can produce spurious associations in observational data. Here we present CauTrigger, a hierarchical deep latent variable model that integrates do-calculus to identify potential causal triggers and predict perturbation outcomes across multiple regulatory layers. By disentangling causal and spurious latent factors, CauTrigger recursively reconstructs the underlying regulatory hierarchy and enables interpretable reasoning from observational data. Across synthetic and real-world datasets with multilayer regulatory structures, CauTrigger outperforms existing methods in identifying causal triggers and forecasting system-level responses. Applied to single-cell multi-omics and gut microbiome datasets, CauTrigger prioritizes candidate causal triggers and uses in silico perturbations to generate testable hypotheses about biological state transitions and inform potential strategies for state navigation. Together, these results establish CauTrigger as a general-purpose framework for causal discovery in complex biological systems.

Article.ArticleTitle: Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Prioritizes Candidate Paraptosis-Related Genes in Painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy.

Abstract.AbstractText: Painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy (PDPN) is among the most disabling complications of diabetes, but its molecular features and underlying biological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Paraptosis, a non-canonical form of programmed cell death characterized by endoplasmic reticulum/mitochondrial swelling and cytoplasmic vacuolization, is associated with endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondrial stress, processes that are also implicated in diabetic neuropathy, but its potential involvement in PDPN remains unclear. This study applied an exploratory integrative strategy that combined peripheral blood bulk transcriptomic data from 12 patients with PDPN and 12 healthy controls, together with publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from human peripheral nerve tissue (GSE266026), comprising samples from patients with DPN and traumatic limb amputation (TLA) comparators. Candidate genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes with a paraptosis-related gene set, and were prioritized using LASSO, SVM-RFE, and random forest. The biological context of the prioritized genes was further explored through immune infiltration analysis, two-sample Mendelian randomization, single-cell characterization, and scTenifoldKnk-based computational virtual knockout analysis. Fifteen paraptosis-related differentially expressed genes were identified, with a significantly elevated paraptosis-related score in PDPN. AKT1, CASP9, and EIF2S1 were prioritized by all three machine-learning methods. Computational immune-cell deconvolution estimated increased the estimated neutrophil abundance and decreased the estimated CD8⁺ T-cell and resting memory CD4⁺ T-cell abundance in PDPN blood, with distinct correlations between the three candidate genes and inferred immune-cell profiles. Mendelian randomization provided evidence consistent with a potential association between genetically proxied higher AKT1 expression and diabetic polyneuropathy risk. Single-cell analysis revealed cell type-specific expression patterns of the three candidate genes, while computational virtual knockout analyses predicted gene-regulatory perturbations involving immune-inflammatory, neuronal structural, and cell-adhesion pathways within the respective network backgrounds. This exploratory integrative analysis prioritizes AKT1, CASP9, and EIF2S1 as candidate paraptosis-related genes associated with PDPN and provides a biological context for further mechanistic and experimental investigation.
